verdict: Caution on merchant/SPV solar exposure in Anantapur; lend only to EPC and O&M contractors with NTPC REL work orders and back-to-back payment terms, avoid pure merchant IPPs and module traders.
title: Anantapur renewables: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A solar project here is land plus evacuation plus a 25-year offtake contract; the cash comes from the PPA, not from the panels.** NTPC REL has just tendered an EPC package with land for up to 1200 MW (900 MW + 300 MW) ISTS-connected ground-mounted solar near its Anantapur project, bids closing 27 November 2026 [3]. That is the single live fact in this city right now, and it tells you the money this year sits with contractors, not generators. Local coverage of Anantapur itself is thin beyond this tender [1][2], so lean on first principles and peer results.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in land aggregation, evacuation and EPC execution; cash sits one step behind the PPA.** Bid security alone is ₹50 crore for 900 MW, ₹20 crore for 300 MW and ₹100 crore for full capacity [3], so the EPC bidder must fund serious margin money before a rupee of revenue. On the operating side, tariffs are single-part, so revenue moves with generation and weather [9], and floating-rate term loans reset regularly [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the PPA tenure against debt tenure and the P-90 PLF assumption; if the PPA lock-in is shorter than the loan, ask what happens at renewal and at what tariff [11].

## What has changed now
**Peer results say volumes are strong but margins are being competed away.** Suzlon grew revenue 26% to ₹4,869 crore in Q2 FY27 with record 710 MW deliveries, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.8% from 18.6% [4][5]. Waaree faces lower module utilisation and softer module prices [7], while GK Energy grew H1 FY27 revenue 38.9% to ₹907.8 crore and is diversifying into rooftop and a 150 MW/300 MWh BESS order [6]. Read together: order books are healthy, pricing power is not. So price the EPC contract, not the pipeline.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue EPC contractors and O&M vendors with a signed NTPC REL award, and land aggregators with clear title and encumbrance-free transfer.** The tender explicitly requires encumbrance-free land including BESS land and three years of O&M [3], so those are bankable cash flows. **Avoid merchant IPPs without a PPA, module traders holding inventory into falling prices [7], and any SPV whose sponsor cannot show PPA renewal history [8].** Collect from customer: contract value, payment milestones, retention terms and promoter net worth.

## Structure, covenants and early warning
**Structure to the milestone, not the balance sheet.** Release against commissioning certificates, keep retention until performance testing [3], and take a DSRA. Covenant DSCR at 1.10x with a cash trap below it, as rating agencies use [10]. Every month take generation/PLF data, PPA counterparty payment status, land title updates and module price movement. Watch for: bid security funded by borrowed money; PLF below design P-90 [11]; PPA tariff renegotiation talk; and any request to extend retention.
watch: PLF below design P-90 for two quarters -> freeze further disbursement and re-run DSCR
Receivable ageing beyond 60 days -> ask for DSRA top-up
Quarterly land title and encumbrance certificate
Any encumbrance or title dispute -> stop release of next milestone
Monthly module price and inventory statement
Inventory holding beyond 90 days into falling prices -> reduce drawing power
DSCR below 1.10x -> trigger cash trap per covenant [10]
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
